body:
@cghislai apart from the regression (?) that you are seeing here- what would be the case for having an empty event handler? I mean - if you don't take any action on a given event, why adding `(fileread)` at all?

I would say that in this case we should simply throw a good error, but maybe you've got a valid use-case?

It was an hack.
I had a filereader that read the file then stored the dataURI in a field. I had an img component with the src attributed bound to that dataURI field. The issue was that the img was not reloaded once the file was read. Triggering that event triggered change detection and the image was updated.

I now moved that job in a Promise, and update the dataURI field in the then clause, and image updates automatically.

OK, so from what I understand it was simply a way of hacky way of kicking-off change detection, right?

If so, let's solve this issue by introducing better checks / error messages for missing event handlers. How does it sound?
Sounds good. That was the main point of this issue.

issue.title: directive with "[on-*]" selector
issue.body:
Upgrading my app from alpha34 to alpha35, one directive I had with a selector `[on-init]` was not working anymore. I realize it must be conflicting in the parser with the canonical syntax for events, but it was working until alpha35 and the error we have now is not really explicit:

```
TypeError: Cannot set property 'lastInBinding' of undefined
at Function._ConvertAstIntoProtoRecords.create (http://me:8080/jspm_packages/npm/angular2@2.0.0-alpha.35/src/change_detection/proto_change_detector.js:97:39)
at http://me:8080/jspm_packages/npm/angular2@2.0.0-alpha.35/src/change_detection/proto_change_detector.js:35:47
```

Maybe the error could be more explicit and the doc warns about not using these prefixes (`on`, `var`, `bind`) in attribute selectors?

issue.title: local variable undefined in html template
issue.body:
Hello,

Looks like local variables are broken in alpha-22. 

This simple code:

``` html
<input #newtodo type="text" (keyup)/>
{{newtodo.value}} 
```

is throwing following exception:

```
TypeError: Cannot read property 'value' of undefined in [
    {{newtodo.value}}
     in MyAppComponent]
```

It was working previously in a version bundled with quick start project.

What is interesting it is that it doesn't work only for, lets call it, bind operations. When I pass local variable to as a parameter to an event, then everything is working:

``` html
<form action="#" (submit)="add(newtodo)">
    <input #newtodo type="text" (keyup)/>
```

body:
So how would we go about specifying where we need change detection? Working with simple view locals this can be very handy: ``` html
``` In earlier versions I was using this "hack" to trigger change detection based on events. Now I can't do this anymore unless I would like to update my directive model, which sometimes I might don't want to when working with simple view locals. Is there an other best practice I'm missing here? Cheers
@gionkunz you should be using `ng-model` here - there is no point in accessing DOM properties if you are interested in the input's value.

@pkozlowski-opensource Actually it's debatable if that feature was "hacky". I actually really liked to specify what events on an element causes change detection. It was explicit but also flexible. Also this is whats (maybe still and shouldn't) listed on this example: https://angular.io/docs/js/latest/guide/user-input.html#local-variables
Right - we should definitively update examples then.
